newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gabon deal lifts Energy Africa to new high.
newsitem.headline: Gabon deal lifts Energy Africa to new high.

text.p: Shares in Energy Africa Ltd jumped nearly 11 percent on Thursday following overnight news that it had secured the rights to almost all of the current oil exploration acreage in the Republic of Gabon.

But despite the share's leap to a fresh record high of 20.50 rand, a gain of 200 cents or 10.8 percent, dealers on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange were cautious, saying volumes were thin and that investors remained wary of exploration stocks.
"The share looks like it is being pushed by speculators...there is no investment interest," one dealer said, adding that the deal was more bullish for Energy Africa parent Engen Ltd.
"Energy Africa has had a great performance for the past eight months rising from about 12 rand...(but) it is giving Engen, which has had a rough time, scope to move up."

By 1015 GMT, shares in Engen, which owns 60.51 percent of Energy Africa, added 70 cents or 2.7 percent to 26.30 rand, its best level in three months. Energy Africa stocks had slipped off their highs to 20.10 rand after only 30,100 shares had traded.
Energy Africa said on Wednesday it had acquired the right to participate in six potential development projects and 22 exploration projects in the African country.

John Bentley, Energy Africa's managing director, declined to pin a price to the deal, but said the cost of the acquisition and projected development costs could readily be met from its existing cash resources.
